## 1. Background
Industrial IoT deployments generate high-dimensional multivariate sensor streams. Kim et al. (2023) survey 112 IIoT anomaly-detection systems and find that transformer models now account for 38% of published approaches, up from 9% in 2020.

## 2. Reconstruction and association-based methods
Anomaly Transformer (Xu et al., 2022) introduces association discrepancy. TranAD (Tuli et al., 2022) reports F1 of 0.815 on SWaT and reduces training time by up to 99%. GTA (Chen et al., 2021) learns graph structure among sensors and reaches F1 0.91 on SWaT.

## 3. Contrastive and general-purpose backbones
DCdetector (Yang et al., 2023) leverages dual attention mechanisms to capture both local and global temporal dependencies and employs contrastive learning to learn robust representations without the need for reconstruction. TimesNet (Wu et al., 2023) demonstrates state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmark datasets for anomaly detection.

## 4. Domain applications
Okafor et al. (2022) apply a transformer encoder to vibration data for rolling-element bearing fault detection, achieving 97.4% accuracy on the CWRU dataset and detecting faults on average 6.2 hours before failure. Lindqvist et al. (2021) deploy attention-based models on SCADA data from 48 wind turbines, reducing false alarms by 41% relative to threshold-based monitoring.

## 5. Open challenges
Label scarcity, concept drift, edge deployment constraints, and evaluation protocol issues: the widely used point-adjust protocol can inflate F1 substantially, so we recommend reporting both point-wise and event-wise metrics.

import pytest
from decimal import Decimal

from ledgerly.money import Money
from ledgerly.refunds import RefundLine, compute_partial_refund, compute_full_refund


def test_full_refund_usd():
    lines = [RefundLine("A1", 2, Money(Decimal("19.99"), "USD"))]
    assert compute_full_refund(lines, "USD").amount == Decimal("39.98")


def test_refund_partial_jpy():
    # issue #312: 1000 JPY item, 15% discount, refund 1 unit -> 850 JPY
    lines = [RefundLine("J9", 3, Money(Decimal("1000"), "JPY"), Decimal("15"))]
    assert compute_partial_refund(lines, {"J9": 1}, "JPY").amount == Decimal("850")


def test_refund_partial_multi_currency(fx_fixture_2024q3):
    # EUR invoice refunded and settled in USD at the fixture rate
    lines = [RefundLine("E2", 4, Money(Decimal("10.99"), "EUR"), Decimal("12.5"))]
    got = compute_partial_refund(lines, {"E2": 1}, "EUR", settle_currency="USD")
    assert got.amount == Decimal("10.45")
    assert got.currency == "USD"


def test_refund_more_than_purchased_raises():
    lines = [RefundLine("A1", 1, Money(Decimal("5.00"), "USD"))]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        compute_partial_refund(lines, {"A1": 2}, "USD")
